packageRules.description: third_party/ holds unpacked crates.io releases patched for collaboration (#1043; third_party/README.md). Their manifests mirror the upstream release, and their dev-dependencies are never built by the workspace, so a bump there proves nothing and drifts the vendored copy from the release it names. Update them by re-vendoring.

Hold the GitHub-hosted runner at ubuntu-24.04. On ubuntu-26.04 (#872) the GUI smoke suite fails wholesale: dogtail stops finding the apps' push buttons over AT-SPI ('New Document', 'Close', 'Add sheet'), and test_gui_harness.py's process-ownership test kills a process it did not start. Moving runners is a migration of the GUI harness, not a version bump. Remove this rule in the PR that makes the suite pass on 26.04.

Keep the Lifafa CI container on a released Fedora. docker.io/library/fedora:46 is Rawhide (its dnf installs from the rawhide repo) until Fedora 46 ships in spring 2027; #2092 ran the Lifafa job on it and it failed. Raise the bound to <47 when Fedora 46 is released.
Hold the rdocx family at 0.16.2 until the Letters adapters support 0.16.3, and group the eventual upgrade so incompatible partial updates are not proposed (#1725).

dcp-matrix (both copies) computes Synapse's registration MAC with Hmac<Sha1>, so hmac and sha1 move together: each digest release line (hmac 0.13 with sha1 0.11 on digest 0.11) only accepts its own hash types, and a lone bump of either does not build (#2138, #2144).
Lifafa (lifafa/, its own lock): html5ever and markup5ever_rcdom move together, because RcDom implements only its own html5ever release's TreeSink, so a lone html5ever bump does not build (#2060).

Lifafa's toolkit follows the suite's: lifafa/ links suite-common (INTEGRATION-PLAN C1), which pins gtk4 0.11 and libadwaita 0.9, so a Lifafa-only bump of gtk4, libadwaita, webkit6, pangocairo or cairo-rs puts a second GTK or cairo in its graph and does not build. They move together with the root workspace's gtk-rs bump, by hand, re-resolving lifafa/Cargo.lock in the same change.
Lifafa's IMAP worker uses imap-proto types that async-imap 0.12 reshaped; hold at 0.10 until the worker is ported (#1986).

Lifafa's mail reader, PGP path and attachment renderer use mail-parser 0.9's part offsets and charset decoders, which 0.11 changed (u32 offsets, private decoders); hold until that port lands as its own change (#2066).

Never automerge in lifafa/. Its build job is path-filtered, so it is not a required check, and an automerged bump can land red: #2060, #2066 and #2067 did. A person merges Lifafa updates once that job is green.

The p2panda crates move as one: tools/collab-spike/dcp-p2p pins all six at one version, so a lone bump never resolves. 0.8 reshapes the store, spaces and signing APIs the binding uses; hold below it until the port (#2084).

dcp-streams (both copies) stays on reqwest 0.12. Its transport trusts only the CA it is given, over rustls with ring (`rustls-tls-manual-roots`, `tls_built_in_root_certs(false)`), and collab-spike.yml's tree gate bans aws-lc-rs and rustls-platform-verifier. reqwest 0.13 drops that feature and builder method, and both of its rustls features pull rustls-platform-verifier (`rustls` adds aws-lc-rs too). Moving it is a TLS-stack decision (a preconfigured ring ClientConfig, and the gate), not a version bump.

Mandelbrot (mandelbrot/, its own lock): let a crate release age a few days before proposing it, so yanked or quickly patched releases never reach a pull request. 'strict' holds the branch back until then instead of opening it with a pending check. Folded in from mandelbrot/renovate.json, which Renovate does not read in a subdirectory.
Mandelbrot: ruma is re-exported by matrix-sdk, and bumping it alone puts two ruma-common versions in the graph, so the two move together.

Mandelbrot: gtk-rs and the bindings built on it (gstreamer-rs, libadwaita, libshumate, sourceview5, glycin, aperture) all depend on one glib; bumping one alone either fails to resolve or puts two glib versions in the graph.
Mandelbrot: the LiveKit SDK and the libwebrtc bindings it pins move together.

Mandelbrot: no check exercises a call inside the app, so its matrix-sdk/ruma and LiveKit bumps stop for a person (mandelbrot/docs/DEVELOPMENT.md, 'How we know an update works'), and so does anything in its MatrixRTC engine or e2e stack, whose harness is path-filtered and cannot be a required check.
publish-mandelbrot.yml only runs on mandelbrot-v* tags and by hand, so no pull-request check exercises a bump there.
